text: 67-year-old male. The patient complains of a 2-month history of generalized fatigue. He mentions no specific triggers but notes that the fatigue has been progressively worsening. He denies any recent infections, significant weight loss, or night sweats.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) and Serum Ferritin. Have you noticed any changes in your appetite, taste, or bowel habits over the past two months?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 8.3 g/dL (low), WBC: 81,000 /mm3 (elevated), Platelets: 35,600 /mm3 (low), Serum Ferritin: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Leukemia. The combination of severe anemia, significantly elevated white blood cell count, thrombocytopenia, and normal ferritin indicates a bone marrow failure process, likely leukemia, rather than iron deficiency. I recommend an immediate peripheral blood smear and bone marrow biopsy to confirm the specific type.
